bull.b: Oruka's very low leverage and large equity base provide durable financial flexibility to fund clinical programs without immediate refinancing risk. This balance-sheet strength supports multi-quarter R&D execution, partnering optionality and strategic discretion during pivotal readouts.

Robust Phase 2a efficacy and safety data materially de-risk Oruka's lead dermatology program, enabling Phase 3 planning and strengthening the case for best-in-class positioning. Durable impact includes improved partner interest, clearer regulatory path and higher probability of later-stage success.

Clear shareholder approval of directors and governance items provides management continuity and reduces activist or governance disruption risk. Stable leadership and broad investor alignment support consistent long-term strategy execution and smoother decision-making around partnerships and financings.

bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow at near -$90M TTM signals meaningful ongoing funding needs. Over multiple quarters this pressure can force dilutive financings or urgent partnering, constraining long-term capital allocation and increasing execution risk if clinical timelines slip.

Being pre-revenue with expanding net losses means profitability remains distant and company value hinges on clinical success. This structural profile amplifies binary pipeline risk and makes multi-quarter operational planning dependent on financing or near-term positive readouts.

Contractual dosing restrictions materially constrain ORKA-001's ability to pursue inflammatory bowel disease indications for several years, narrowing near-term addressable market and complicating partnering or deal structures. This durable legal constraint could reduce optionality and commercial upside.
